title: Sticky Offers & Card Tags
subtitle: Making urgency readable at a glance
summary: An offer can be time-limited, new, limited in stock, from a partner, or usable several times, often all at once. I designed a tag system for offer cards so members can see what matters, and what's about to expire, before opening anything.

problem.statement: Offer cards had to show several conditions at once. Without a system, every combination would be designed on its own and the most urgent detail, like an expiry date, could get lost.
problem.bizCtx: Offers live in the member wallet and on the home screen, across 13+ brands running on one design system. If a member misses an expiry date, both the member and the brand lose out.
problem.constraints: Cards are shared components themed per brand, so tags had to read on any photo and any brand colour. Some offers exist as several instances with different expiry dates.

contribution.summary: I mapped every combination of offer conditions and designed the card, tag and stamp card system to cover all of them.
contributions: Mapped the real combinations of offer conditions, from “expiry only” to “expiry + new + limited + usage”, and designed a card for each.
Set tag order and placement: validity top right, New as an accent pill below it, usage count on the left.
Handled multi-instance offers: the badge shows the earliest expiry across instances (“Next expires …”).
Extended the same visual language to stamp cards, with a redeem state when the card is full.

findings.finding: Time-limited offers are the most common
findings.evidence: In the combination matrix, expiry-only is the most common case.
findings.implication: Validity gets the same fixed top-right slot on every card.

findings.evidence: Combinations like expiry + new + limited stock + usage exist in the product.
findings.implication: Tags stack in a set order instead of competing for the same space.

findings.finding: One offer can have several expiry dates
findings.evidence: Multi-instance offers each carry their own validity.
findings.implication: The card shows the earliest date, phrased as “Next expires”.

insight.decision: A small, ordered set of tags in fixed positions, so any combination reads the same way on every card and every brand.

design.solution: Each card pairs a photo with a title and a short line of context. Tags sit on the photo in a fixed order: validity first, then New, with usage count and stock limits placed so they never collide. Stamp cards use the same card shell with a photo background and a clear redeem state.

image.alt: Offer card variants with different tag combinations, and a stamp card.

design.flows: Members scan the offers list, see what's new and what's expiring, and open a card to use it. Stamp cards fill up with purchases and switch to a redeem state when complete.
design.annotations: Photos and copy in these images are placeholder coffee shop content, since the real cards are themed per brand. The tag rules are the same for every brand.

outcome.shipped: Designed as part of the MyLoyal component library: card variants for each tag combination, the offers list and the stamp card redeem state.
outcome.measures: Measures that matter: how many offers are redeemed before they expire, and fewer member questions about when an offer ends.
outcome.learnings: Mapping every combination up front was faster than solving cards one at a time, and it exposed the multi-instance case early.
